audience.programmeDescription: Study programming, statistics and AI alongside questions about rights, governance and society. Groningen teaches this degree in English at Campus Fryslân in Leeuwarden.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Groningen example follows AI and Society. The UCR options emphasize social applications and ethics, or cognition and the ways people and machines interpret information.

cellNotes.text: Both develop programming skills. UCR focuses on Python and computational problem-solving.
Both study how data are organized and retrieved. UCR focuses on relational modeling and SQL.
Both use visualizations to explore and communicate data. UCR also teaches data cleaning and analysis.
Both use statistical and machine learning methods for prediction and model evaluation.
Both develop neural network methods, from foundational architectures to more advanced applications.
Both develop probability and statistical inference.
Groningen combines data science and its social context in one introductory course.
Groningen has a dedicated big data analytics course. UCR develops advanced analysis through machine learning and neural networks.
Groningen studies the rhetoric of data graphics. UCR develops visual analysis and data visualization in separate settings.
Groningen has a dedicated advanced programming course. UCR develops programming through several computational courses.
Both examine foundations of human rights. UCR covers general rights theory and legal protections.
Both examine AI ethics and public consequences, including fairness, privacy and accountability.
Both apply research and data analysis to business questions. UCR focuses on customers and markets.
Groningen studies science and technology as social practices. UCR addresses social institutions and technology across courses.
Groningen continues its science and technology studies sequence.
Groningen has a dedicated course on governance of innovation.
Groningen studies responsibility in innovation. UCR addresses related questions through AI ethics and organizational study.
Groningen applies human rights to digital impacts in a second dedicated course.
Groningen applies data science directly to social problems. UCR develops data analysis and social research through separate courses.
Groningen studies sustainability in its innovation-governance sequence.
Groningen studies AI regulation as a dedicated subject.
Groningen uses a dedicated simulation exercise. UCR applies computational models to decision problems.
Groningen applies advanced AI to problems such as language modeling. UCR also studies text classification and generation in its neural networks course.
Groningen has a dedicated human–machine interaction course. UCR studies related questions through cognition, perception and AI.
Both develop research design. UCR includes measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments.
Groningen requires a 10 EC field project.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for an approved minor.
Groningen requires a 15 EC thesis. UCR’s optional research element is outside the scheduled degree.

notes.text: Groningen combines data science with dedicated courses in digital rights, innovation governance and human–machine interaction. It also requires a field project and a thesis.
Groningen allocates 5 EC to research design and project management and 15 EC to the thesis.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
BENENTR212.text: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Students develop a strategic plan, from vision to execution, and identify digital value opportunities. Using industry cases, they gain foresight into digital technologies and their impact on strategy, business models and social responsibilities.

BENENTR311.name: Market Research
BENENTR311.text: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t. You’ll plan and carry out real research, analyze what you find, and share your results. Our course shows you how to gather opinions and turn them into smart business ideas—perfect for future marketers, analysts, or entrepreneurs.

source.reviewNote: Compared the retained modal with the revised official description. The revision adds promotional wording without changing the substantive account of planning, conducting and analysing market research; the existing concise text remains faithful.

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.text: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.text: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.text: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

DISARIN311.text: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

An experience report connects engagement or observation to course concepts, while an individual project uses theoretical and empirical sources to analyse a civil-society organisation, movement or initiative.

HCBCOGN112.text: Neurobiology studies nervous systems and behaviour through comparative anatomy, evolution and physiology. Students examine animal behaviour, research models, welfare and research ethics, then connect biological rhythms and regulatory behaviour to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders. Comparative-anatomy work and a literature-based report apply neurobiological concepts.

Topics include attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control, social cognition, pain and consciousness. An attentional-blink experiment and a team research proposal develop engagement with empirical research, experimental design and ethical reflection.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
